title: Pipeline pattern: chained stages with correct closing

videos.script: The last pattern joins the others into a chain. A pipeline is a row of stages, each one a goroutine, each joined to the next by a channel. {{stages}} You build two stages, one that produces numbers and one that squares them, and chain them by calling one with the other. Then you time five items through two slow stages. Two hundred milliseconds of work finish in one hundred and twenty, because every stage works at once. {{closing}} Next, shutting down. Each stage closes the channel it sends on, after its input has closed, and the close travels down the chain. A slow stage can be widened with three goroutines inside, and it still closes once. {{cancel}} Last, the reader that leaves early. Two results out of a thousand, and two stages are stuck for ever. A context in every send lets them stop. Closing flows with the data. Cancelling flows against it. {{close}} Lesson 16 is the tool that checks all of this: the race detector.
